visual.evidence: In the wide low-angle forest-path shot (frames 21-40), the small dog and the cyan wisp run down the centre while the giant's limb is otherwise out of frame. At frame 22 (2.2 s) only tree trunks with flared root bases are visible at top-centre - no foot. At frame 23 (2.3 s) a large three-lobed/toed giant foot first appears at the top of frame, its toe tips at their lowest position relative to the distant ground line (≈ upper-third), i.e. the settled/impact pose. Through frames 24-30 the same foot rises and shrinks (toe tips move from ≈0.35 to ≈0.25 of frame height) and is gone by frame 31, which is the subsequent lift, not the landing. The earlier close-up of the dog (frames 0-6) shows a foot already suspended high at the top edge (lifted, no ground contact visible), so it corresponds to the first stomp cycle whose contact is off-screen. Hence the only visually resolvable 'land-and-stop' of the giant foot - the second heavy landing - is the 22→23 transition, bracketed as last-pre-contact (22) to first-contact (23), with the settling phase ending ≈24.
visual.uncertainty: High. The foot is far in the misty background, so exact ground contact cannot be crisply resolved; the 'stop' is inferred from the foot's lowest toe position at frame 23 versus its rising trajectory in 24-30. An alternative reading is that frames 21-22 already show the foot planted (the central column mistaken for a tree), which would shift the contact bracket to [20,21]; and another is that 23-30 is a descent rather than a lift, which would push first contact to ≈30. The vertical trajectory of a small, hazy limb at 10 fps is ambiguous, and no debris/camera-shake cue confirms the impact frame. The close-up segment (0-6) contains no visible contact at all, so it is excluded from the second-landing bracket.
